criterion_notes.c1: Assesses the district-level multidimensional sustainability status of clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision in Soppeng Regency via expert appraisal rather than examining household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study includes a 'Law and Institutional' dimension (9 expert-scored attributes such as availability of water management legislation, customary/religious law instruments, stakeholder communication networks, and inter-regional management) and tariff items ('PDAM water tariff', 'price discrimination among and within consumer groups') as inputs to a 48-attribute sustainability index, which could broadly touch governance/institutional factors (though even under the plain wording the paper is still excluded overall for lacking a service-access outcome). Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, Criterion 2 is 'no' because none of these items is examined as a rule-type mechanism governing household or community service access; they are merely unanalysed expert-scored inputs aggregated into a treatment-plant sustainability index, with the sensitive legal/institutional attributes being stakeholder communication networks, periodic consumption analysis, and inter-regional integrated management.
criterion_notes.c3: Uses primary empirical expert-appraisal data collected via survey, in-depth interviews, and observation of purposively selected experts, analysed with Multidimensional Scaling (Rap-IPABSoppeng / RAPFISH), leverage analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation (though expert sample size is not reported).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports only composite sustainability index percentages (45.64% multidimensional index and five dimension sub-indices) for IPAB provision and root-mean-square leverage sensitivity of attributes to those index scores; reports no empirical outcome on household or community water access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Does not identify an analytical exposure-to-access-outcome relationship at household or community level, and does not report the sample size or composition of the expert respondents or raw attribute values.

evidence_quotes.quote: this research was conducted to measure the sustainability of the provision of clean water treatment plants (IPAB) in Soppeng District.

This study was conducted using a survey method through in-depth interviews and observation techniques. Respondents were taken by purposive random sampling with criteria of experts who have expertise in accordance with the field under study

Based on the results of leverage analysis, attributes that are sensitive to the value of the economic dimension of the sustainability dimension are obtained (1) price discrimination between and within the consumer group, (2) availability of funds for the development of clean water, (3) contribution to the sector utilization of water sources to GRDP, and (4) percentage of poor population.

Based on the results of leverage analysis, attributes that are sensitive to the legal and institutional dimension of the sustainability index are obtained, namely (1) communication networks between stakeholders in the development of the clean water sector, (2) implementation of periodic clean water consumption analysis, and (3) integrated management, sharing or merger between regions.

The results of the multi-dimensional sustainability Rap-IPABSoppeng analysis in Soppeng Regency for the provision of clean water treatment plants based on existing conditions, obtained a sustainability index value of 45.64% and included in the less sustainable status.

raw_response.exposure: 48 expert-scored attributes across five sustainability dimensions (environmental, economic, social, infrastructure and technology, and legal and institutional); no specific legal or administrative exposure governing access isolated
raw_response.outcome: Composite multidimensional sustainability index (%) of clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision (45.64% overall) and root-mean-square attribute leverage sensitivity
raw_response.population_and_sample: Clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision system in Soppeng Regency, South Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, evaluated by purposively sampled experts (number of respondents not reported)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E04 - Wrong outcome; also fails C1, narrow C2, and C5). The study applies a RAPFISH-derived multidimensional scaling rapid appraisal (Rap-IPABSoppeng) of expert opinion scores across 48 attributes in five dimensions to compute a district-level sustainability index (45.64%) for clean water treatment plant (IPAB) provision in Soppeng Regency, Indonesia. It reports no empirical outcome measuring household or community water access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion, nor does it evaluate a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing access (under either the 2026-10-13 narrow reading or, given the absence of any service-access outcome, the plain Criterion 2 reading).
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional expert rapid appraisal survey analysed via Multidimensional Scaling (RAPFISH / Rap-IPABSoppeng), leverage analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation
